raw_response:
I'll answer in character as this farmer.

**My reasoning:**

I have been farming these 30 mu for 35 years, so I know what works here in Quzhou. My father planted garlic, my neighbors plant garlic, and it brings good money — so I keep 5 mu for garlic every year. It is hard work but my wife and daughter-in-law help in the harvest. Garlic needs heavy fertilizer and lots of water, I know this from experience.

The biggest piece of land, 20 mu, I do wheat and then maize, same as everyone around me. This is the safest way. Wheat goes in October after maize harvest, maize goes in June right after wheat. The well is close so I can water when I need to.

Cotton I keep only 5 mu now. Cotton is too much trouble — many times spraying for bollworm, picking by hand, my back is not what it was. But the price is still okay and I know this crop well.

For fertilizer, I buy the compound fertilizer (diammonium, 15-15-15) at the township dealer, and urea for topdressing. I use a bit more than the bag says — if I put too little and the wheat turns yellow, I lose much more than the cost of one extra bag. My neighbor Old Wang uses about 3 bags compound plus 1 bag urea per mu for wheat, I do similar. A bag of fertilizer is 50 jin, I count in bags not kg but I know one bag urea is about 22 kg N.

For garlic I put the most fertilizer because garlic eats a lot. I also put some chicken manure I get cheap from my nephew's farm.

I use improved seed for wheat (Jimai type) and hybrid for maize — the seed dealer brings good varieties each year and my neighbors test them. I still plow deep before wheat, rotary for the others.

Water: wheat needs 3-4 times (winter water, green-up, jointing, filling). Maize usually 1-2 times if rain is short. Garlic needs 5-6 times, very thirsty. Cotton 2-3 times.
